Header:
Date: 2027-10-03 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Eli Torres (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Lena Ortiz (Aurora SRE), Mark Hsu (Aurora Platform), Priya Rao (Aurora CTO)
Recording ID: ff-20271003-aurora-01

Summary (auto):
Postmortem follow-up for 2027-09-29 incident where Aurora saw degraded inference throughput and increased tail latency on Redwood Hosted. Discussion covered immediate mitigations, long-term reliability improvements (Dedicated capacity, KV cache tuning), security/compliance ask list, and next steps for benchmarking/contract.

Topics:
- Incident recap and root-cause hypotheses
- Mitigations applied and short-term improvements
- Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs and pilot scope
- Observability and runbook updates
- Security/compliance artifacts and audit path

Transcript:
00:00:03 Maya Chen: okay good afternoon everyone thanks for making time. we wanted to run through the incident follow-up, recap what we saw on the 29th and go through a plan to prevent recurrence and next steps for the pilot.
00:00:12 Priya Rao: thanks maya and thanks redwood for jumping on this quickly. the outage hit our triage system and it's uh, it's had a real impact on response times. we need concrete mitigations and a timeline.
00:00:25 Eli Torres: yeah absolutely, priya. quick recap from our side — we correlate increased tail latency with evictions in the KV cache during a burst of large-context requests. when the cache thrashes, we saw excessive GPU work per request which pushed our queuing.
00:00:40 Mark Hsu: just to add, our traffic pattern had a spike in multi-segment documents around 11:10 UTC, we were at 3x normal qps for ~7 minutes. that seems to be the tipping point.
00:00:55 Maya Chen: okay so hypothesis is cache eviction + burst + batching behavior. eli, can you summarize the kernel/serving signals you saw?
00:01:06 Eli Torres: sure. the runtime metrics show high tail p99 generation time, increased kernel launches and a rising NVLINK latency. there's also a spike in small-batch sequential dispatches which reduces GPU efficiency; in short, we were doing a lot more small work.
00:01:22 Lena Ortiz: were there any OOMs or container restarts? our side showed some latency-driven backpressure but no pod evictions.
00:01:30 Eli Torres: no evictions observed at the pod level, no OOMs, but ephemeral stalls due to synchronous KV loads. also the model variant fallback was triggered for some routes which increased tokens per request.
00:01:45 Priya Rao: okay that fallback behavior is concerning — it should only trigger under sustained capacity pressure. is that a misconfiguration?
00:01:52 Eli Torres: possibly. our routing policy uses a cost-latency fallback. during the burst the primary model hit queueing SLO so policy routed some requests to a higher-latency but cheaper variant which ironically increased work because of context handling differences.
00:02:08 Mark Hsu: that sounds like a policy edge case. can you share the exact policy rules and logs?
00:02:14 Maya Chen: yes we'll share the policy dump and routing logs. samir will also get the incident timeline and the original alert dumps.
00:02:21 Samir Patel: i'll assemble the timeline and alerts and put them in the shared drive by end of day.
00:02:28 00:03:05 Maya Chen: short term mitigations we applied the night of — we increased prefix cache TTL, temporarily pinned hot prefixes, and disabled the automatic fallback policy for affected routes. those brought queues back to acceptable levels.
00:03:20 Lena Ortiz: pinned prefixes helped. we saw p99 drop from 1.2s to 320ms for the first 10 minutes after the change.
00:03:28 Eli Torres: for the medium term we recommend Dedicated pilot with fixed GPU pools plus: KV cache resizing, batching policy changes to avoid small-batch serial dispatch, and a canary for fallback policy that uses token-count-aware decisions.
00:03:45 Priya Rao: we want a clear SLA for p95/p99 and predictable cost. Dedicated sounds promising but we need numbers — what throughput per GPU and expected tail latencies?
00:03:58 Eli Torres: we'll run a targeted benchmark replicating your multi-segment request shape and peak qps. expected throughput depends on model and quantization; for the Llama-variant you're running we estimate 80-120 qps per T4-equivalent GPU in our hosted mix but Dedicated with optimized kernels and batching can push to 150+ qps with lower tail. we'll quantify in the benchmark.
00:04:20 Mark Hsu: please include both int8 and fp16 runs, and a 'cold start' case for KV cache misses.
00:04:27 Eli Torres: yes will do.
00:04:34 00:05:05 Lena Ortiz: on observability, we need per-request token-level breakdowns and correlation with KV hits/misses. current dashboards aggregate too much.
00:05:15 Samir Patel: noted — we'll add a per-route dashboard with token breakdown and a KV hit/miss heatmap. we'll also surface kernel launch rates and NVLINK latencies.
00:05:28 Priya Rao: security/compliance — we still need the SOC2 pack and SSO/SAML mappings for our auditors. also KMS integration questions for key custody.
00:05:40 Maya Chen: samir will own sharing the SOC2 artifact set. for KMS we support AWS KMS and HSM integrations for our Private offering; we'll document options and what data flows are covered.
00:05:53 Samir Patel: i'll share the audit pack and a short note on the KMS flow by next week.
00:06:00 00:06:30 Eli Torres: one more operational mitigation — introduce burst-protection throttles on the ingress with token-bucket limits per-customer route to avoid sudden multipliers in qps overwhelming cache. it adds graceful degradation instead of fallback misfires.
00:06:45 Mark Hsu: that would help our internal rate-limiter too. what about runbook updates?
00:06:52 Maya Chen: we'll add a runbook entry for cache thrash detection, exact metrics to watch (KV miss ratio, small-batch fraction, kernel launch rate) and automatic mitigations (pin prefixes, increase TTL, disable fallback).
00:07:05 Lena Ortiz: can we get example dashboards and alert thresholds?
00:07:09 Eli Torres: yes we will provide recommended thresholds and sample Grafana panels.
00:07:20 00:08:00 Priya Rao: about the Dedicated pilot — what does the onboarding timeline look like and what support do you provide during ramp?
00:08:08 Maya Chen: typical Dedicated pilot is 4-6 weeks: week 1 ingest workloads and baseline, week 2 bench and tune, week 3 pilot traffic, week 4 validation and SLA sign-off. we provide SE support, runbook co-development, and optional on-prem package if you need VPC/isolation.
00:08:26 Mark Hsu: cost model? we need committed pricing and burst options.
00:08:31 Maya Chen: i'll include committed capacity pricing and burst credits in the package we send.
00:08:39 00:09:10 Eli Torres: technical deep-dive note — we found a scheduler corner that favors batching small sequential dispatches. patch in our runtime is straightforward: adjust batching window heuristics and prefer coalesced batches for high-concurrency routes. we'll include a patch note and plan.
00:09:26 Lena Ortiz: will that patch require restarts?
00:09:30 Eli Torres: a rolling restart to pick up the new runtime, but it's non-disruptive with canary first.
00:09:38 Priya Rao: please provide risk notes for the patch.
00:09:41 Eli Torres: will do.
00:09:48 00:10:20 Samir Patel: quick question — did we confirm whether any PII was in the requests during the incident? our logs showed redacted fields but we want customer confirmation.
00:10:30 Lena Ortiz: we redacted everything but i will confirm with legal and send a note.
00:10:36 Priya Rao: we did have some user identifiers but no raw PHI; still want to be conservative.
00:10:43 Maya Chen: understood, add that to the audit pack and we'll ensure retention policies are respected.
00:10:51 00:11:25 Mark Hsu: ok let's recap next steps before we wrap. eli, bench plan and traces; maya, pricing and Dedicated pilot contract; samir, SOC2/KMS docs and timeline; lena, request shapes and SLO targets.
00:11:40 Eli Torres: i'll run the benchmarks and aim to have preliminary numbers and traces by 2027-10-07.
00:11:47 Maya Chen: i'll send the pricing and pilot paperwork by 2027-10-06.
00:11:52 Samir Patel: i'll drop the SOC2 pack and KMS note by 2027-10-08.
00:11:57 Lena Ortiz: we'll provide sample requests and peak windows by 2027-10-05.
00:12:05 Priya Rao: schedule the on-prem benchmark for week of 2027-10-11, please add an optional all-hands with our legal team if necessary.
00:12:15 Maya Chen: noted, we'll propose three slots.
00:12:20 00:13:00 Maya Chen: any other concerns or questions from aurora?
00:13:05 Lena Ortiz: just one — can you guarantee fallback won't be re-enabled automatically without a safe-guard?
00:13:12 Eli Torres: we'll change the default to manual enable for that policy and add a token-count threshold so it won't misfire.
00:13:20 Priya Rao: fine, thanks.
00:13:25 Maya Chen: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and sync mid next week. appreciate the partnership.
00:13:35 Mark Hsu: thanks all, bye.
